To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Pneumocystic pneumonia (PCP) is an important opportunistic infection in HIV and other immunosuppressed patients in India.
Pneumocystic jirovecii is the most prevalent type of Pneumocytic pneumonia in immunosuppressed patients and the most prevalent genotype is genotype 2.
the most prevalent P. jiroveii genotype in India is type 2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first report on genotyping of P. jrovecii isolates from India based on sequence variation at mt LSU rRNA.
the prevalence and distribution pattern of genotypes in India, a country with the third largest population of HIV-infected individuals.
the genotypic diversity of P. jrovecii in HIV-infected individuals and in immunosuppressed patients from the Indian sub-continent.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no specific P. jirovcii genotypes associated with HIV infection.
the mt LSU r RNA gene is a useful marker in the study of genotypes of the P. jiroveii in India.
the prevalence of genotypic distribution is not significantly different in HIV-infected individuals as compared to non-HIV-infected individuals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most common genotype of P. jirouvecii in India is type 2, followed by genotype 3, genotype 4, and genotype 1, respectively.
genotype 2 is the predominant genotype in HIV and non-HV immunocompromised hosts in northern India.
genotype 1 is the most prevalent in immunocompromized patients in northern India.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the most prevalent Pneumocystic genotype is not the same across the world.
the most prevalent genotype in India is different from the most prevalent genotype observed in other parts of the globe.
the mt LSU rDNA gene is a suitable marker to genotype P. jiroveii in India.
